content.text: {"answer":"The supplied papers do not seem to address “fairness limits” directly. They focus on LLMs, knowledge graphs, personas, personalization, privacy-preserving user modeling, and governable personalization in recommender systems, but not on formal fairness limits or impossibility results.\n\nThe closest result is a discussion of transparent, privacy-preserving, and governable personalization, including accountability and user control in LLM-agent recommendation settings [8]. Other papers mainly propose recommendation architectures and report performance gains, such as constrained knowledge fusion with bounded performance degradation [4], privacy-preserving personal knowledge graphs [2], and persona- or graph-based personalization methods [1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10].","grounded":false}
